entries.summary: A deliberately bounded executable subset covers root and embedded subprocess scopes, none start/end events, generic tasks, normal/conditional/default sequence flows, exclusive routing, parallel split/join epochs, Standard Loops, FixedMultiInstance/1 and CollectionMultiInstance/1 on generic Tasks, and CatchEventChoice/1 Message/Timer waits. Multi-Instance profiles freeze one bounded closed member set, while catch waits open exact arms and atomically record one deterministic winner, continuation, loser cancellation, and Message delivery disposition. Causal replay reconstructs both families without rerunning their decisions. Fingerprinted budgets bound Timer lexical bytes, execution-state bytes, and transition-journal count/bytes beneath fixed hard ceilings. SubProcess or CallActivity multi-instance execution, progressive behavior events, partial output, open/draining groups, checkpointed long histories, and the broader BPMN Event lifecycle remain unsupported.

entries.summary: FixedMultiInstance/1 executes a bounded cardinality-based generic Task profile. It evaluates loopCardinality exactly once at activation, freezes stable item:index identities, supports sequential and parallel scheduling, records exact active/completed/terminated counters over generated instances, and routes once after an all join or the first true completionCondition. That condition terminates already generated active members while a sequential planned suffix is durably marked not-generated and is not included in runtime instance counters; stale completeTask commands are fenced and idempotent. Boundary Error and terminal business-failure paths cancel the generated group before routing or failing, and the journal replays every transition exactly. XML v6 represents broader collection and behavior metadata, but collection execution belongs to the separately evidenced CollectionMultiInstance/1 profile and behavior remains All.

entries.summary: CollectionMultiInstance/1 executes a bounded collection-driven generic Task profile without treating the source as a mutable queue. One exact externally compiled binding for loopDataInputRef is evaluated once at activation and its canonical JSON array is frozen with source indices, order, and duplicates intact. A scalar inputDataItem explicitly opts into current-item mapping. Complete output gathering requires loopDataOutputRef, a scalar outputDataItem, a matching collection-valued Task DataOutput, and a protocol-v3 Task binding; codec-validated outputs are gathered by source index, and empty input yields an empty output array. Output gathering with completionCondition is rejected until a partial-result policy exists. Data, evaluator, collection, and Task bindings plus all collection/item/output limits are fingerprinted. Parallel all-join mode supplies bounded WCP14 evidence. The pure kernel does not require Effect Workflow; its native bridge is optional and separately tested. Progressive behavior, SubProcess/CallActivity Multi-Instance, streaming manifests, open WCP15 creation, WCP34/WCP36, and complete Process Execution Conformance are not claimed.

entries.summary: CatchEventChoice/1 executes normal-flow standalone Message and timeDuration/timeDate Timer Intermediate Catch Events. Exact external Message bindings commit an ordered non-empty key-correlation expression, payload contract, and authorization-policy build. The atomic delivery transition is the acceptedAt authority: it requires every previously unseen receipt value to equal services.now while it validates the exact active arm and selects or fences the delivery; sender time is never authoritative, while exact redelivery of an already committed receipt remains idempotent. Timer expressions evaluate to strings that the profile parses as a bounded ISO-8601/XML Schema duration or dateTime subset; this is a runtime profile check, not an XSD restriction on tExpression text. The execution-global deliveryId ledger consumes both Message winners and Timer-preempted Messages. Journal replay reconstructs the recorded correlation, deadline, consumption, continuation, fences, and ledger without clock or expression reexecution. The profile rejects operationRef even though BPMN Table 10.99 requires it for executable Processes, selects only exact key correlation from the §13.3.3 alternatives, and excludes early-message retention, timeCycle, Signal/Conditional/Multiple Events, Start/Boundary/Receive/event-subprocess catches, and the broader Event lifecycle. This is an executable implementation slice, not Process Execution Conformance.

entries.summary: CatchEventChoice/1 executes an exclusive non-instantiating Event-Based Gateway with bounded unique unconditional direct Message/Timer catch branches. Every arm opens in one atomic wait group. The atomic delivery transition requires every previously unseen receipt.acceptedAt to equal services.now and compares that authoritative instant with every materialized Timer deadline; exact redelivery of a committed receipt is idempotent. Timer wins equality, the earliest eligible Timer wins regardless of which Timer woke the run, and equal deadlines use immutable branch ordinal. Winner routing, continuation, and cancellation of all losing arms and Timers commit together. Current-time late/stale ingress is fenced, backdated ingress is rejected, Timer-preempted deliveryId values remain globally consumed, and causal replay verifies rather than reexecutes the race. The optional native adapter delegates one deferred per wait group, absolute DurableClock scheduling, and post-commit wake/recovery; its typed first-wins wake is not the BPMN winner. The host must persist its caller-owned workflowName/executionId address, the token is not a credential, and reliable post-crash notification requires a host outbox or equivalent because the adapter implements no persistence, transport authentication, correlation, or outbox authority. Memory evidence is not persistent/cluster conformance. Receive Task branches, conditions/defaults, other events, and instantiating/Parallel gateways remain unsupported, so this is not the complete Event-Based Gateway surface or Process Execution Conformance.

entries.summary: CatchEventChoice/1 supplies the bounded transient Message/Timer form of WCP16 Deferred Choice. All exact arms become enabled together only after the Event-Based Gateway is reached. One atomically timestamped Message delivery or eligible Timer wins deterministically; the delivery transition requires acceptedAt to equal services.now, and its continuation and withdrawal of every loser commit atomically. Timer wins equality, equal Timers use immutable branch order, late and duplicate delivery is fenced, and replay consumes the recorded race facts. Persistent or early trigger retention, human work, Receive Tasks, Signal/Conditional/Multiple Events, and broader Event-Based Gateway modes are not claimed.
